## Summary

ProxyOpenAIChatCompletion never checked whether the caller's Claude
subscription was exhausted before injecting credentials, unlike
ProxyMessages (#519). On an OpenAI-wire turn routed to Anthropic, this meant
a spent OAuth token was dispatched instead of falling through to the
deployment/BYOK key. The subscription-only 402 guard had the same gap.

Full root-cause analysis and original live evidence: #761

## Fix

Two changes in ProxyOpenAIChatCompletion, both mirroring ProxyMessages
exactly:

1. Suppress an exhausted Claude subscription before credential resolution:
   ```go
   if s.claudeSubscriptionExhausted(ctx, r.Header) {
       ctx = withSuppressedClaudeSubscription(ctx)
   }
   ```
2. Extend the subscription-only refusal guard to also check observed
   exhaustion, matching service.go:2373's exact composition:
   ```go
   if !servedOnSubscription(ctx) || s.anthropicSubscriptionObservedExhausted(ctx, r.Header) {
   ```

## Known composition gap (documented, not fixed here)

Messages' subscription-only guard is additionally gated by
`&& !routeRes.UsageBypass`; this PR doesn't add that exclusion on the
OpenAI side. Verified this is inert today: usageBypassEngaged and
anthropicSubscriptionObservedExhausted read the identical usage-observer
snapshot (usage_bypass.go:93 and :136), so UsageBypass=true and
observed-exhausted=true cannot coexist — structurally, not just
empirically. Revisit when bypassToAnthropic/UsageBypass consumption is
wired on this surface (separate, not-yet-filed issue).

## Tests

- `TestOpenAI_SubscriptionExhausted_ServesOnDeploymentKey`
- `TestSubscriptionOnly_OpenAI_ExhaustedSubscription_Refuses402`

Both fail on main, pass on this branch. Landed in `usage_bypass_test.go`,
reusing existing fixtures (`bypassScorerPickMdl`, `bypassSubToken`, `fakeRouter`,
`fakeProvider`) rather than new mocks.

## Live verification (re-run against the actual committed diff, not a
local patch — git diff HEAD was empty throughout)

| Check | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| Credential at dispatch (OpenAI) | spent OAuth token | none — deploy key |
| Mock-Anthropic round trip | 3 attempts, 429 to client | 1 dispatch, 200 to client |
| Subscription-only + exhausted | 1 dispatch, spent OAuth, no refusal | 0 dispatches, ErrCreditsExhaustedSubscriptionUnavailable |

## Test plan

- [x] Both new tests fail on main, pass on this branch
- [x] `make check` green
- [x] `go test ./internal/proxy/... -race` clean except pre-existing `TestFireTelemetryRecoversFromPanic` flake
- [x] Existing Codex subscription-only coverage (`subscription_only_openai_test.go`) unaffected
- [x] Live credential / 429 / subscription-only repros re-run against committed `59966cc`

Fixes #761

## Summary

Rebuilds the BuildWise Business Plan into a professional, submission-ready **30-page** report generated from a single shared content model, rendered to both **DOCX** and **PDF** so the two stay identical in structure and content. Output files are updated in place (`BuildWise_Business_Plan_Report.docx` / `.pdf`) — no duplicate/versioned reports.

### What's included
- **30 pages exactly** (verified in the PDF): cover, declaration & acknowledgement, table of contents, Chapters 1-15, and references. Every chapter starts on a fresh page.
- **43 navy-themed diagrams** (`buildwise_diagrams.py`): vertical/serpentine flows, timelines, radial infographic, Business Model Canvas, SWOT matrix, 2x2 positioning & risk matrices, funnel, value pyramid, org chart, doughnut/bar/line charts, and a monitoring dashboard.
- Consistent corporate **navy (#163A70)** theme, navy-header tables with alternating shading, KPI cards, callout/insight boxes, service cards, sequentially numbered figures, and bottom-centre page numbers (declaration = Page 1, matching the TOC).
- Cover uses Times New Roman (DOCX renders it natively) and an embedded serif for the PDF so the Rupee symbol renders correctly.

### Architecture
- `report_content.py` - single source of truth (ordered content blocks).
- `render_pdf.py` (reportlab) and `render_docx.py` (python-docx) - two renderers over the same model.
- `buildwise_diagrams.py` - matplotlib figure generator.
- `build_report.py` - one-shot orchestrator (`python build_report.py`).
- Removed the superseded markdown->converter pipeline (`md_to_docx.py`, `md_to_pdf.py`, `make_charts.py`, `Business_Plan_Report.md`, old chart PNGs).

### Tested
- Full rebuild via `build_report.py` runs clean; PDF verified at **30 pages** with all 31 embedded figures auto-numbered sequentially (Figure 1-31, no gaps).
- DOCX validated structurally (2 sections: unnumbered cover + numbered body, 31 embedded figures, chapter page breaks). Rendered PDF pages spot-checked visually (cover, TOC, exec summary, business model canvas, financials, org chart, conclusion).

### Known limitations
- LibreOffice/Word is not available in the build environment, so the DOCX could not be rasterized here for a pixel-exact page-count check; the PDF is the pixel-faithful proof of the shared content, and the DOCX enforces the same structure via explicit page breaks (Word may shift a page due to native Times New Roman metrics).
- To fit exactly 30 pages, a curated subset of the 43 diagrams is embedded (the rest remain available in `figures/`); embedded figures are numbered sequentially so there are no gaps.
- Cover course line uses "Entrepreneurship and Family Business Management" (consistent with the declaration text).

## Why

**Finding B1 of the PR #37 post-merge audit — the single MANDATORY-before-re-bless item for the v0.2.1 tag** (report: `2026-07-16_pr37-w7-post-merge-audit.md`).

Running it as written would have dropped `baseline.json` from **14 scenarios / 7-member gate_set to 3 / ~2**, silently erasing 11 scenarios including 5 of 7 gate members — after which Lane R's `--compare` reads `pass_rate=None` for the erased scenarios and goes permanently blind to regressions on 11 of 14 while exiting 0. ## What

  - WARNING when a reused record's scenario file was edited since (version drift → needs its own recapture); records for deleted scenario files dropped with a note; WARNING when a recapture replaces scored records with all-SKIP/ERROR
  - a capture covering every prior scenario stays a fresh overwrite (with a printed reminder that prior `_provenance` is not carried)
- **`checkpoint.py`** — warns before writing a checkpoint that would stomp scored committed records it has no trials for (same failure through the side door: pointing the crash-safe checkpoint loop at a partial-recapture run). No behavior change.
- **`compare_against`** — `guidance_hash` joins `model_id`/`cli_version` in the replay-lane exclusion (audit Axis-2 minor "guidance_hash false-refuses Lane R replay compare"): replay injects no guidance, but `build_identity` re-reads `guidance.md` on every lane, so every `guidance.md` edit false-refused the compare permanently (#37's guidance edit was the first trip). Model-lane compares still refuse on guidance_hash drift.
- **Tests**: new `tests/test_capture_merge.py` — 8 KB-free tests pinning the merge contract (subset preserves non-swept records + recomputes sets; disclosure + provenance carry; full capture stays fresh; no-prior fresh; version-drift warning; stale-record drop; reused incomplete checkpoint record stays incomplete; all-SKIP stomp warns). +2 compare tests in `test_identity_tiers.py` (replay excludes guidance_hash → rc 0; model lane still refuses → rc 3).

| In-situ `--compare` at HEAD | refuses ONLY on the legitimate post-W7 `tool_inventory_hash` drift (17→18) — the honest §7 refusal the queued re-bless clears; `guidance_hash` no longer contributes |

Committed `baseline.json` is untouched by this PR.

author: jpmorard
body:
## Summary

- harden concurrent AGI runtime, cleanup, deployment, service-loop, worker-host, settings, sidecar, navigation, and hosted-view ownership boundaries across threads and processes
- make cleanup proof-based and fail-closed: retain exact leases, Futures, process groups, tokens, state, and PID evidence until termination/publication is durably proven
- add bounded lock, Windows sharing-retry, transactional config/state publication, and crash-recovery contracts for mutable shared files
- make DAG submission/execution idempotency transactional and immediately recoverable after finalization failures
- isolate Streamlit session environments and temporary import state; make ANALYSIS preparation own and terminate its complete process tree
- confine worker cleanup/kill paths to validated runtime roots while preserving sibling evidence and legacy bootstrap compatibility
- preserve dependency-light base-package imports and reconcile the upstream inference-page deletion across package, robot, capability, and docs contracts

## Repro

Before this change, concurrent or interrupted callers could reproduce one or more of these failure classes:

- lifecycle, cleanup, or service operations could release a lease while an exact worker, Future, child process, or state file was still live or unreadable
- a fast-exiting `uv`/shell wrapper could disappear from the job list while a Dask or environment-preparation child survived in the owned process group
- service restart/start publication failures could leave live loop Futures whose exact keys were never durably recorded
- repeated cancellation or a stalled lock could freeze peers indefinitely or strand an owned cleanup task
- Windows file-sharing denial could turn valid config/state into an apparent absence, lose an update, or fail a replace without bounded recovery
- a failed target cleanup could erase or resurrect sibling PID evidence, or an unsafe worker target could reach process discovery/deletion
- concurrent settings, dotenv, app pages, or hosted inline imports could overwrite newer state or leak process-global environment/import state
- DAG finalization failure could retain ambiguous ownership and block immediate exact retry
- clean Python 3.13/3.14 base imports could cross into the optional UI environment

The regressions exercise these interleavings directly, including delayed releaser versus successor publication, corrupt/unreadable state, partial service replacement, state-write failure, wrapper exit with a surviving child, inaccessible process evidence, repeated cancellation, PID reuse, sibling cleanup, Windows sharing denial, and DAG post-callback finalization failure.

## Root Cause

The affected paths mixed process-local locks, mutable singleton/class state, check-then-act filesystem operations, best-effort cancellation, and non-generation-scoped cleanup. Several recovery paths treated cancellation, absence, age, a closed wrapper, or a moved marker as sufficient proof without retaining the exact owner generation or proving that worker-side execution had ended. Mutable state publication was not consistently transactional or retryable under Windows sharing semantics. UI and evidence surfaces also mutated process-global or shared filesystem state without a bounded session/process ownership contract.

## Regression Test

- runtime/service tests cover exact loop-Future keys, partial start/restart, durable publication failure, legacy state recovery, lost clients, repeated stop, full-runtime fallback, cancellation, and lease retention
- real process tests cover fast-exiting wrappers, surviving descendants, process-group TERM/KILL, unreaped parents, inaccessible recent same-user candidates, and retry-safe cleanup
- cleanup/CLI tests cover path confinement, traversal/symlink rejection, production `cwd == target` kill geometry, PID incarnation, sibling evidence, rollback, and pre-install legacy bootstrap execution
- `agi-env` tests cover bounded constructor/current/reset/session locks, non-overlapping singleton initialization, transactional settings/dotenv, Windows sharing retry, sidecar ownership, and hosted-render exclusion
- Analysis/UI tests cover owned preparation trees, time-bounded interruption, transactional settings helpers, session-local environments, and cross-page/app behavior
- DAG/evidence tests cover durable ownership, exact retry, compare-and-swap transitions, immutable snapshots, atomic latest pointers, and Windows directory/file sharing behavior
- base-import tests prove `agilab.lab_run` imports without optional `agi_env` on Python 3.13 and 3.14

## Validation

- full AGI GUI workflow parity: **3,680 passed, 5 skipped**
- full shared-core tree: **1,479 passed, 5 skipped**
- full `agi-env` tree: **957 passed, 1 skipped**
- final core/runtime/service/cleanup/CLI/Analysis integration slice: **524 passed**
- changed public/UI/DAG/evidence slice: **387 passed, 1 skipped**
- complete views slice: **305 passed**
- Flight runtime/form/cluster regressions: **109 passed**
- DAG/idempotency/evidence slice: **106 passed, 1 skipped**
- strict shared-core typing: **21 source files, no issues**
- dependency policy: **28 passed**
- clean base-package imports: Python **3.13.14** and **3.14.6**
- staged impact validation, ANALYSIS maintenance memory, provenance guard, Ruff, compile, and diff checks: passed
- GitHub CI: passed, including Windows core, local-only policy, docs guard, Python 3.13/3.14 compatibility, GitGuardian, and clean public installs on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows

Known baseline: the impact-inferred narrow slice passed 274 tests and hit only `test_setup_pycharm.py::test_gen_app_script_preserves_builtin_app_venv_bindings`; the same failure was reproduced unchanged on clean `origin/main`, so it is excluded as unrelated. The generated built-in-app recommendation for `flight_telemetry_project` is not runnable because that app is not registered by `tools/builtin_app_tests.py`; the actual affected Flight regressions passed as listed above. Windows-only skips remain covered by the Windows CI matrix.

# Summary

Pedido do Caio (triagem dos emails de erro de 16/07): **14/07 a quota diária do Resend estourou** (avisos de 80% e 100% com 3s de intervalo) e todo envio seguinte do dia foi dropado — inclusive **email de produto pra usuário real** (digest, régua de consentimento), o canal primário de ativação (pilar 6). Emails de admin competiam pela mesma quota sem teto agregado.

- **Migration 0129** `admin_alert_email_log` — contador diário **persistido** (☑ aplicada e verificada em prod nesta sessão). Contador em memória reseta a cada deploy do Railway — armadilha #54, o mesmo bug que a 0119 corrigiu no throttle da escalação.
- **`services/email/adminAlertBudget.ts`** — `tryClaimAdminAlertBudget(kind, ref)`: cap por classe (`bug_alert` 10/dia, `reconciliation_escalation` 10/dia), janela = dia UTC (reset do Resend), claim-before-send (mesmo padrão do CAS da 0119), fail-open em erro de DB (blip não silencia o canal de alerta).
- **`bug-reporter.notifyByEmail`** — capped → só loga; a issue do GitHub (registro durável) nunca é suprimida.
- **`reconciliationCron.maybeEscalateByEmail`** — budget checado **antes** do CAS semanal da conta: capped não queima a janela de 7 dias, o próximo run re-tenta em horas.

## Análise de root cause

1. **Classe:** "email de admin é ilimitado e compete pela mesma quota diária do email de produto" — o dedup por hash do bug-reporter limita POR BUG (não o agregado, armadilha #50) e o throttle da escalação é por conta (não cross-conta).
2. **O fix fecha a classe?** Sim pros dois produtores existentes, via um helper único que qualquer produtor futuro de alerta consome (cap por classe no mesmo lugar). Produtor novo que NÃO usar o helper reabre a classe — mitigado pela doc do módulo; gate mecânico (lint "todo sendEmail pra ADMIN_EMAILS passa pelo budget") ficaria caro pra 2 call sites, reavaliar na 3ª ocorrência (armadilha #51).
3. **Teste da próxima variante?** 8 testes unitários do budget (cap, corrida, janela UTC, fail-open, cap por classe) + 1 teste por produtor (capped → sem email, issue preservada; capped → CAS semanal intacto).
4. **Efeito colateral?** Pior caso: alertas de admin silenciam APÓS o 10º do dia por classe — mitigado porque o registro durável (issue bug-auto) nunca é suprimido e a supressão loga `admin_alert_email_capped`. Corrida entre reports concorrentes pode passar 1-2 do cap (contagem não-atômica) — aceito, o teto protege contra dezenas, não exige exatidão. **Instrumentação:** N/A na UI (sem superfície nova visível); observabilidade server-side pelo próprio `admin_alert_email_log` (é o log do canal, padrão da regra) + logs `admin_alert_email_capped`.

author: marcelxpfeifer
body:
## What and why

The assistant's AI-SDK `ToolSet` was a map literal built inline in the
conversation runner. PP-11 promotes it to a **hosted registry**
(`TOOL_MODULES`): each built-in is a module pairing the AI-SDK tool with the
metadata the host enforces around it — an optional feature flag, a data-access
scope, an LLM spend-attribution tag, and a scrub policy — the same shape as the
other hosted-module registries (send transports, agent steps, draft strategies,
autonomy gates).

`buildAssistantTools(ctx)` now assembles the set from the registry: it
**flag-gates membership** (a tool whose flag is OFF is omitted — the model never
sees it) and **wraps every scrub tool so the host injection-scrubs its output**
before it can reach a prompt. The host scrub is a blanket guarantee on top of
the per-field scrubbing the tool bodies already do — it covers fields a tool
leaves unscrubbed (e.g. `draftEmailReply`'s `recipient`, `searchEverything`'s
`url`) and any future plugin tool that forgets to scrub.

Built-in membership, ordering, spend tags, error semantics, and feature-off
behavior are unchanged. No built-in declares a flag, so the assembler does no
flag I/O for the shipped set — the assembled `ToolSet` is byte-identical to the
old literal, in the same order.

The registry contract and the pure host helpers live in a new
`assistant/toolRegistry.ts` (no `'use node'`, no AI-SDK runtime import) so they
unit-test as plain functions; the tool builders and the ctx-bound assembler stay
in `assistant/tools.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria → where satisfied

- **Replace the literal tool set with hosted modules carrying flag, scope,
  spend, and scrub metadata** — `HostedAssistantToolModule` in
  `assistant/toolRegistry.ts`; `TOOL_MODULES` in `assistant/tools.ts` declares
  all seven built-ins with `{ flag?, scope, spend, scrubOutput, build }`.
- **Preserve every built-in exactly (membership, ordering, defaults, error
  semantics)** — `buildAssistantTools` emits modules in declaration order and,
  with no flagged module, does zero flag I/O; the tool bodies are unchanged
  (same internal queries, clamps, per-field scrubs, spend calls). Pinned by the
  "built-in tool registry conformance" and "buildAssistantTools" suites
  (exact name+order, scope ∈ read/draft, draft-only spend tag, all scrubbed,
  none flagged) and by the pre-existing `assistantRunner`/`chatAssistant`
  integration tests which still pass.
- **Prove unauthorized/unsafe tool outputs cannot enter prompts** —
  feature-off omission is proven by `selectAssistantToolModules` +
  `buildAssistantTools` flag-gating tests (flag OFF or absent ⇒ tool omitted);
  unsafe output is proven by `scrubToolOutput` + `withHostScrub` +
  `buildAssistantTools` tests that an assembled scrub tool's injected output is
  withheld before the model sees it, including a field the tool body never
  scrubbed. A module can only *add* scrubbing; the scope union has no
  write/send member, so no tool can mutate or send.
- **Tool output is untrusted plugin text: clamp and injection-scrub it; host
  re-scan and autonomy gates stay outside tool implementations** — host
  injection-scrub via `withHostScrub`/`scrubToolOutput`; clamps stay in the tool
  bodies; the runner's downstream re-scan/gates are untouched.

## Test evidence

- `npx vitest run` on the new `assistantToolRegistry.unit.test.ts` (16 tests)
  and the existing assistant suites (`assistantRunner`, `chatAssistant`,
  `assistantPrompt`, `assistantConversations`) — all pass.
- `bun run ci:verify` — green (typecheck, full `@owlat/api` vitest suite of
  428 files / 5173 tests, lint incl. `check-codegen`, plugin graph + boundary
  checks, format ratchet).
- `turbo build --filter='!@owlat/desktop'` — 12/12 tasks successful.
  (`@owlat/desktop` build needs `cargo`, unavailable in this environment and
  unrelated to this change; it is excluded from the CI test/verify matrix too.)

## Plan-drift notes

- The plan (line 523) says "the same shape as `STEP_MODULES`". Agent-step
  modules are data-only descriptors with an `exportPath` to trusted bundled
  code, because steps run in a separate reauthorized pass. Assistant tools have
  no such indirection — the executable IS the AI-SDK tool closing over the
  runner's ctx — so a built-in module carries a `build(ctx)` function instead of
  an `exportPath`. Metadata fields (flag/scope/spend/scrub) match the plan.
- No built-in is independently flag-gated today (the assistant as a whole is
  gated by `ai.assistant` upstream), so all built-ins leave `flag` undefined to
  preserve behavior exactly. The `flag` field and the assembler's gating are the
  seam plugin-contributed tool packs will use; the flag-resolution path reuses
  the existing `internal.workspaces.featureFlags.getResolvedFlags` query and is
  exercised via the injectable `modules` parameter in the assembler tests.
- `scope` is modeled as `workspace:read | workspace:draft` (the two built-in
  classes) rather than a retrieval contact-scope, so a conformance test can
  assert no built-in carries a write/send scope.

author: jeiang
body:
## Summary

Since the SeaORM 2.0 migration (d1294f3), `atticd` crashed at startup in every integration test, so the `basic-*` matrix could not pass at all. This PR fixes the two runtime regressions and two latent test bugs uncovered once the tests could actually run:

- **Run database migrations on a single connection** — SeaORM 2.0's migrator no longer pins one pooled connection; with a multi-connection SQLite pool, consecutive DDL statements can observe stale schema state and the migration chain fails nondeterministically on a fresh database (`no such column: temp_nar_id`, `there is already another table or index with this name: nar`). `run_migrations` now forces a single-connection pool (the API server's runtime pool is unaffected). Includes a regression test running the full chain against a fresh file-backed WAL SQLite database, which reproduced the failure reliably.
- **Set an explicit postgres username in the integration tests** — sqlx 0.9 no longer derives the username from the OS user when the URL omits it (it falls back to `whoami`, which yields `anonymous` inside the hardened systemd unit), breaking peer authentication. The `localhost` authority is a parser-required placeholder; the `host` query parameter overrides it with the Unix socket path (verified against sqlx 0.9's parser).
- **Fix over-escaped newlines in the cache-list assertions** — `"test\\nzebra\\n"` inside a Nix indented string reaches the Python test script as a literal backslash-n, so the assertions could never pass. They were merged while atticd was crashing at startup, so they had never executed. Expected outputs verified against a live `atticd` + `attic` CLI session.
- **Run one-off `atticd` commands as the service user** — the GC subtest invoked `atticd --mode garbage-collector-once` as root, which now fails postgres peer auth with the explicit username. It runs through `systemd-run` with the service's `DynamicUser`/`User`/`StateDirectory`/`EnvironmentFile` properties, mirroring the module's `atticd-atticadm` wrapper.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p attic-server` on this branch standalone (15 tests, including the new migration regression test)
- Full integration matrix on a NixOS machine: `basic-{sqlite,postgres}-{local,garage}` all pass (~80 s each). Before this PR, all four failed at atticd startup.

body:
## Logging overhaul: unified levels, structured QC/diagnostics output, end-of-run summaries

  Brings the pipeline's logging up to a consistent, operator-readable standard end
  to end — from per-module stage summaries through QC/diagnostics keyword output to
  a compact per-run verdict — and codifies the conventions in the governing docs.

  ### What changed

  **Level discipline & recoverable conditions**
  - Recoverable/degraded runtime conditions now emit `logger.warning(...)` instead
    of `warnings.warn` — unlike `warnings.warn`, `logger.warning` doesn't dedup per
    call-site, so a per-frame condition is recorded every time (DRP-RUN-08).
    `warnings.warn` is reserved for developer-facing deprecations/API misuse, and
    `setup_logging` still funnels any third-party/stdlib warning into the log via
    `logging.captureWarnings(True)`.
  - De-flooded the level pipeline: inner-loop (per-order/-chip/-frame) detail moved
    to `DEBUG`, so `INFO`/`WARNING` stay scannable.
  - Test warning assertions migrated from `pytest.warns` to `caplog`, and the
    now-obsolete `filterwarnings` ignores (PROGID/KOAID/masters-naming) dropped.

  **Quality-control suite logging**
  - Diagnostics → DEBUG per metric; QC → one line per flag as
    `keyword = value — comment` (FITS comment read off the header), DEBUG on pass /
    WARNING on fail; checkpoints → INFO roll-up, a cross-level `ISGOOD=0` WARNING
    listing the failing flags, and ERROR on a hard-checkpoint raise.

  **Per-module & per-run summaries**
  - Each module's end-of-`perform()` summary gains blank-line padding (baked into
    `_info`, so the `logger.info` call stays clean) and drops the redundant
    `summary:` prefix, making stage boundaries easy to spot by eye.
  - RadialVelocity surfaces the combined science RV (RV/RVERR/BJD_TDB) in its
    summary headline.
  - New end-of-run verdict block at each recipe's completion — inputs, masters,
    outputs, ISGOOD, combined RV, elapsed — read straight off the finished L4
    (science) or what was stacked (masters). Formatters live in `recipes/_logging.py`
    (`science_run_summary` / `masters_run_summary`), keeping `kpfpipe/utils/logger.py`
    pure logging-setup infrastructure.

  **Packaging**
  - `recipes*` added to `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]`, mirroring `scripts*`, so
    `from recipes._logging import …` resolves from any working directory. Recipes
    and scripts now run from outside the repo root; the recipe entry files remain
    path-selected/exec-loaded (nothing imports them as `recipes.kpf_drp_*`).

  ### Governing-doc updates (please review)
  - **Style guide (§B.2, §6):** documents the level discipline, the no-`print()`
    rule (interactive `info()` excepted), the `logger.warning` vs `warnings.warn`
    split, the QC/diagnostics keyword-log format, and the updated `_info`/summary
    idiom.
  - **Architecture:** recoverable conditions use `logger.warning`; `captureWarnings`
    role clarified.

  ### Testing
  - Full fast suite green (1334 passed); recipe integration suites (33) pass;
    `recipes._logging` import + recipe exec-load verified from a non-repo-root CWD;
    ruff clean.

body:
**⚠️ This PR contains the actual no-BUY fix — #34 and #35 were merged before these commits landed on the branch.**

## Root cause (verified against the live engine)

The nightly calibration fit stored `α=0.9672, β=0, γ=−2.6675` (fit_at 2026-07-16 02:17 UTC). At FULL consensus that curve tops out at σ(α+β+γ) = 15%, clamped to the 0.50 floor — so **every ticket reads exactly 50% calibrated probability and no verdict can pass any gate**. Live NVDA probe: five engines unanimous, agreement 1.0, calibratedProb 0.50, STAND_ASIDE. That is why no BUY has appeared since ~2 AM, including the platform's own suggested names.

## Changes

**1. Calibration validity guards (server, needs deploy)**
- `_shared/calibration.ts`: a stored fit is used only if it can express p ≥ 0.60 at full consensus; degenerate fits are logged and the priors take over.
- `calibration-fit`: the same check at write time — a rejected fit is reported and the stored row heals back to priors instead of persisting the poison.
- Migration `20260716230000`: one-time heal of the currently poisoned row (RLS correctly blocks anon writes, so it ships via the pipeline).

**2. Client-side recalibration (works the moment the frontend deploys — no server deploy needed)**
- `repairDegenerateCalibration()` in DirectProfitMode: fires only when the stored map is provably non-discriminating (server says ≤ 50.5% for inputs the documented priors σ(3.2·|score| + 1.4·agreement − 0.7) map to ≥ 60%). Re-runs the decision-theoretic gate (p ≥ 53%, E[R] ≥ 0.05R after tails and costs, engine/agreement/bucket support) on the engine's raw ensemble and promotes a passing WAIT ticket to the consensus direction using the engine's own entry/target/stop. Self-disables when the server fit heals. Every repaired ticket carries a `recalibrated` marker and a dedicated audit row (stored → prior probability).
- Replayed against the live NVDA payload: 0.50 → 0.95, gate E[R] = 1.83, verdict BUY with the engine's plan, E[π] +4.12/share.

**3. GitHub Actions deploy pipeline restored**
- `deploy-supabase-functions.yml`: deploys all edge functions (honoring `config.toml` verify_jwt) on merge to main or manual dispatch, then invokes the freshly deployed `calibration-fit` once to heal the DB row. Requires a one-time `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` repository secret — note the July 12 run shows green but **silently skipped** its deploy steps because the secret was never set; production has never deployed from GitHub.

## Verification

Typecheck clean, all 221 tests pass, production build succeeds. Client repair verified end-to-end against the live production engine response.

author: harrisonaedwards
body:
## Problem

`spelling-mapper.json` maps the British `practise` verb family to the American `practice` forms:

```json
"practise": "practice",
"practised": "practiced",
"practises": "practices",
"practising": "practicing",
```

British English splits the pair by part of speech — `practice` is the noun ("a medical practice"), `practise` is the verb ("to practise medicine"). American English collapses both to `practice`. Oxford, Cambridge and Collins all give `practise` as the British verb form.

So these four entries convert correct British input into American output, which is the opposite of what a US→UK mapper is for. A sentence like "A practising engineer who practised for years" is silently rewritten to "A practicing engineer who practiced for years".

This is the same class as #37 (ton/tonne) and #40 (waggon): a dictionary entry that isn't a US→UK spelling pair.

## Fix

Remove the four mappings.

Removal rather than inversion: `practice` → `practise` is not safe either, since it would corrupt the noun, and noun/verb disambiguation isn't tractable at the word level. Leaving the family alone is correct for British input, and merely leaves an American verb `practice` unconverted — which is not objectively wrong in British usage, just the less formal choice.

## Tests

Adds `TestPractiseFamily` with three tests: the verb forms, the `-ing` form, and the noun.

Full suite passes apart from the pre-existing `test_end_to_end_phrase_in_britfixignore` failure on `main`, which is unrelated (it concerns `program`/`programme`).

author: azarovalex
body:
## Context

Related to #279, which added support for custom-type array fields in `signableHash()`.

## Problem 1: crash on multi-dimensional array types

`encodeType(primaryType:)` builds its list of struct names to render like this:

```swift
var depSet = findDependencies(primaryType: primaryType)
depSet.remove(primaryType)
let sorted = [primaryType] + Array(depSet).sorted()
let encoded = sorted.map { type in
    let param = types[type]!.map { ... }   // force-unwrap
    ...
```

`depSet` (via `findDependencies`/`getParsedType`) already strips array brackets before using a type name as a dictionary key — but the `primaryType` argument prepended to `sorted` is used as-is, brackets and all.

For a normal (non-array) `primaryType` this is harmless, since the raw string already matches a dictionary key. But `encodeData`'s array handling only special-cases a single bracket pair (`components.count == 3`, i.e. `Type[]` or `Type[N]`). A custom-type array field with **more than one** bracket pair (e.g. `"Item[2][2]"`) falls through to the generic non-array fallback, which passes the type string — brackets still attached — straight into `encodeType`. `types[type]!` then force-unwraps `nil` and crashes.

**Fix:** strip brackets from `primaryType` the same way the rest of the function already does for its dependency set, and replace the force-unwrap with a `guard`/`compactMap` so any type that still isn't found fails to encode that segment instead of crashing.

This doesn't make multi-dimensional arrays *correctly* encode (the underlying array-handling logic in `encodeData` still only understands one bracket pair), but it turns a crash into a normal thrown error from `encodeData`'s existing `guard let valueTypes = types[type] else { throw ABIError.invalidType }`.

## Problem 2: fixed-size struct arrays hash incorrectly

`encodeData`'s two array branches handle `Type[]` (dynamic) and `Type[N]` (fixed) inconsistently:

```swift
// dynamic — hashes each element individually before concatenating
let encoded = try json.arrayValue!.flatMap { try encodeData(data: $0, type: parsedType).web3.keccak256.web3.bytes }
return Data(encoded).web3.keccak256.web3.bytes

// fixed-size — concatenates raw encodeData (no per-element hash!) before hashing once
let encoded = try json.arrayValue!.flatMap { try encodeData(data: $0, type: parsedType) }
return Data(encoded).web3.keccak256.web3.bytes
```

Per [EIP-712](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712), `SomeType[5]` must encode identically to `SomeType[]` with 5 elements — each element gets `hashStruct`'d individually, then the concatenation of those hashes gets hashed once more. The fixed-size branch skips the per-element hash, producing a different (incorrect) result than the dynamic branch would for the same logical data.

I verified this against `@metamask/eth-sig-util`'s `TypedDataUtils.encodeData` (the implementation #279 says it was cross-verified against) using a `Container { items: Item[2] }` example — the real output matches "hash each element, then hash the concatenation," not the current fixed-size branch's behavior. Added `test_GivenFixedSizeArrayOfCustomType_ItEncodesCorrectly`, which asserts against that independently-computed expected value.

## Tests added

- `test_GivenPrimaryTypeWithArrayBrackets_EncodeTypeStripsThemAndMatchesBareType` — direct regression test for the crash fix.
- `test_GivenMultiDimensionalCustomTypeArray_ItThrowsInsteadOfCrashing` — confirms a still-unsupported multi-dimensional array field fails safely (throws) rather than crashing.
- `test_GivenFixedSizeArrayOfCustomType_ItEncodesCorrectly` — regression test for the hashing fix, expected value cross-checked against `@metamask/eth-sig-util`.

All existing tests in `EthereumAccount_SignTypedTests` continue to pass.

body:
## Problem

The `changes` gate in `ci.yml` used `dorny/paths-filter@v3`, which fetches the PR's changed-file list over the **GitHub REST API** on every `pull_request` event (confirmed by the in-file comment and the failing log line `Fetching list of changed files for PR#N from Github API`).

That makes the gate a **single point of failure**: every Rust job is `needs: changes` + `if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true'`, so when the API degrades and the detector errors, all downstream jobs **skip** — one flaky API call blocks 100% of PRs. This is what's currently blocking #117 / #118.

## Fix

Replace the action with a **git-native** detector:
- `actions/checkout@v5` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history)
- compute the `workflows`/`rust` booleans from `git diff --name-only` against the merge-base

No GitHub API call, ever. **Fails open** (runs everything) if the diff range can't be resolved. Drops the now-unneeded `pull-requests: read` scope.

## Validation

- `actionlint` passes (includes shellcheck of the `run:` block).
- Classifier logic dry-run verified for: docs-only, rust src, nested/root `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, workflow YAML, and mixed changes.

- **XSD validation (from #8).** `xmlSchemaValidateFile`'s errors previously went only to libxml2's default stderr handler, invisible to both the thrown exception and this codebase's spdlog logger. Registered `xmlSchemaSetValidStructuredErrors` to capture every error (element name + line) into a new `NML_Parser::last_schema_validation_errors` member, now included in `ingest_file`'s exception message.
- **Unresolved IDrefs / unit errors (from #49).** The unresolved-IDref path was already adequate and left unchanged. Two unit-conversion catch blocks (`apply_fixed_pins`, `resolve_instance`'s numeric-attribute path) logged full context (attribute/element/value) then did a bare `throw;`, losing that context in the exception a caller actually sees — fixed to carry the same context through, with the original conversion error appended verbatim.
- **Unsupported ComponentTypes / silent drops.** `cell_lowering.cpp`'s `lower_on_condition_actions` silently ignored any `OnCondition` child other than StateAssignment/EventOut/Transition — now warns with the cell, OnCondition test, and offending tag. `model_specification.cpp` collapsed "uncataloged type" and "cataloged but Structure-bucket" into one vague message — split into two, the second naming the Phase-3 boundary (ion channels/morphology/biophysical properties). ## Review history

One review cycle, clean pass. Independently verified: the XSD structured-error callback has no use-after-free risk (`this` outlives the synchronous validate call); both unit-conversion fixes throw the same exception type as before (`std::invalid_argument`) with the original error text preserved verbatim, so existing catch sites are unaffected; the `OnCondition` warning and the two-message `model_specification.cpp` split both route correctly (traced the exact conditions); the recording-target warning fires only on genuinely unresolvable paths; every `compile_kernel` call site in `master_kernel.cpp` now goes through the new wrapper (grepped to confirm no bare calls remain); the new compile-failure test triggers a real Metal compiler failure via `xcrun`'s runtime compiler (not mocked) and the thrown message genuinely contains the label, full source, and IR dump; the CUDA-side equivalence claim (NVRTC's `check_nvrtc_compile_result` already throws with the compile log embedded) was independently confirmed by reading `backend.cpp` — no CUDA toolchain available to run it, honestly stated as structural-only. author: rossrdme
body:
## Problem

`lint` flags custom_block `.md` snippet files whose names contain underscores, e.g.:

```
[warning] custom_blocks/Helm_v4_error.md: Bad filename: should be PascalCase —
          rename to "HelmV4Error.md" so it can be used as <HelmV4Error />
```

This is a false positive. The filename becomes a component tag `<Name />`, and the only real constraint is that the name be a **valid JS identifier starting with an uppercase letter**. Underscores are valid identifier characters — `<Helm_v4_error />` is a legal tag. The resolver already agrees: `getKnownComponentNames` registers the raw slug (`names.add(slug)`) as a known component name, so `<Helm_v4_error />` already resolves. Only the filename check was overzealous, conflating "unusable as a tag" with "not my preferred style."

## Fix

Flag a filename only when it *can't* be a component tag — i.e. it's not `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$` (hyphens, or a lowercase initial). Underscores and digits are allowed. When it is invalid, still suggest the collapsed PascalCase form.

## Verification

- Added unit tests: underscore name allowed; hyphenated name flagged; lowercase-initial name flagged. Full suite: **89/89 passing**.
- Ran the patched linter against a real 898-page ReadMe docs repo (Cast AI): the previous `Helm_v4_error.md` "Bad filename" warning is gone, with no new warnings introduced.

Reported via a customer lint run (CX-3425-adjacent). Independent of #33 (Windows path fix).

author: jeiang
body:
## Summary

Implements the low- and medium-risk items from the new `OPTIMIZATIONS.md` (also added here, with the full prioritized list including future work):

**Download path**
- Add `Cache-Control` headers to binary cache responses: content-addressed NAR bodies get `max-age=31536000, immutable`; narinfo and nix-cache-info get `max-age=300`; presigned-URL redirects get `max-age=60`. The `public`/`private` directive follows cache visibility, so shared caches and CDNs only ever store responses for public caches. Enables CDN/proxy offload of read traffic.
- Debounce the `last_accessed` bump to once per hour per object and spawn it off the request path — previously every NAR download awaited a database UPDATE before streaming its first byte (on SQLite, serializing all downloads through the single writer). The timestamp only feeds retention-based GC, which operates at hours-to-days granularity.
- Stream NARs with 64 KiB buffers instead of `ReaderStream`'s 4 KiB default.
- Make the NAR-reassembly chunk prefetch depth configurable (`nar-reassembly-prefetch`, default 4, previously hardcoded 2), improving multi-chunk download throughput on high-latency storage like S3.

**Upload path**
- Skip the redundant SHA-256 pass over in-memory chunks: each chunk was hashed twice over the same immutable server-produced buffer (dedup probe + in-pipeline "verification" that could never fail). Hashing now happens once, inside `spawn_blocking` to keep CPU-bound work off the async executor. Client-claimed hashes (unchunked uploads) keep full in-pipeline verification.
- Batch `chunkref` inserts: instead of one INSERT per chunk (the only per-chunk write for deduplicated chunks), collect them and `insert_many` in the final transaction, in sub-batches of 1000 rows. A failed upload now also leaves no dangling chunkref rows.

**Defaults/config**
- Lower the default zstd compression level from 8 to 3 (compression runs inline in the upload path; level 3 is the standard on-the-fly sweet spot). Overridable as before.
- Make GC storage-deletion concurrency configurable (`garbage-collection.storage-deletion-concurrency`, default 20, previously hardcoded).

New config options are documented in `config-template.toml` and validated (non-zero).

## Behavior changes for existing deployments

- New uploads compress at zstd level 3 instead of 8 (faster uploads, slightly larger files).
- Multi-chunk downloads buffer up to 4 × `chunking.max-size` (~1 MiB at defaults) instead of 2×.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p attic-server`: 21 unit tests + doctest (5 new tests covering the debounce predicate, `cache_control` helper, prefetch validation, and the precomputed-hash compression stream).
- Full integration matrix on a NixOS machine: `basic-{sqlite,postgres}-{local,garage}` all pass with this exact tree, exercising chunked/deduplicated pushes, pulls, and GC on both databases and both storage backends.

Stacked on #15 (the SeaORM 2.0 regression fixes that make the integration tests runnable at all); retarget to `main` once that merges.

body:
## Incident

`data/yahoo/_GSPC.parquet` froze at **2026-06-12** for ~a month while every sibling store stayed current, silently degrading 8 engine consumers: `intl_performance` (the RRG "US vs the World" board on intl.html), `cycle_proxies`, `equity_alloc`, `financial_news`, `intl_claims`, `lab`, `live_overlay`, `signal_lab`.

## Root cause

**^GSPC was never in any `config["yahoo"]["tickers"]` group.** The store exists only because `scripts/spvector_baseline.py` (spvector Phase-0, c3934b9d8d9, 2026-06-14) seeded it once with a one-shot `yf.download` + `store.upsert`. `git log data/yahoo/_GSPC.parquet` shows exactly one commit — it never "broke"; it was never collected.

Why the W0 frozen-tail detector never fired: `collectors/base.detect_stale_series` only inspects **frames a fetch returned** — a series no adapter fetches never appears in any frames dict, so it is structurally invisible. This is the same blind spot already documented (and separately tripwired) for the cboe cor/vol family in `collectors/cboe_indices.check_cor_vol_freshness`.

Not the adjustment-basis guard, not a fetch error — the healed max-fetch agrees with the old seed **byte-identically** (max rel close diff 0.00e+00 over 24,729 overlap rows).

## Fix

- **config.yml** — add `"^GSPC"` to `yahoo.tickers.extras` in the effective top-level yahoo block (~L6205); nightly 1mo upserts resume tonight. (Note: a second, orphaned copy of the old yahoo ticker block sits header-less inside `fred:` at ~L425 — left untouched; dead config.)
- **data/yahoo/_GSPC.parquet** — healed through the adapter's own `_download`/`_extract` path, `period=max`: 24,751 rows, 1927-12-30 → 2026-07-16, overlap verified before upsert; also backfills the dual-basis `close_price` column the one-shot seed lacked.
- **collectors/yahoo.py** — `check_yahoo_freshness()`: store-level NYSE-calendar freshness + row-floor tripwire over a pinned `ENGINE_CRITICAL_SERIES` (`^GSPC`, `SPY`, `^VIX`). Pinned **in code**, not derived from config groups — a config-derived expectation goes blind the moment a name falls out of the list, which is exactly this failure class. Emits NAMED `run_status.json` `stale_series` entries; warn-only, never fails the lane.
- **scripts/collect.py** — run the tripwire after `write_status`, gated on the yahoo adapter being in scope (mirrors the cor/vol wiring).
- **tests/test_yahoo_freshness.py** — clean store / exact ^GSPC frozen-tail repro / stub + missing flags / weekend session-lag tolerance (fake-store idiom, no real `data/` writes).

## Proof

Pre-heal dry-run against the real store:
```
yahoo freshness: ^GSPC — stale: last obs 2026-06-12 is >3 sessions behind 2026-07-16 (age 34d)
```
Post-heal: tripwire clean; `engine.intl_performance._bench_series()` returns 2026-07-16 / 7533.77. `pytest tests/test_collect_identity.py tests/test_yahoo_freshness.py` → 15 passed.

## Interaction with the intl-turns revamp lane

The fail-open SPY substitution in `engine/intl_performance.py` (branch `claude/serene-antonelli-*`, PR from 2026-07-16) is deliberately **not touched** — that fallback stays as belt-and-braces; this PR heals the store underneath it.

Closes plan issue #3318.

## Root cause — not a per-test compiler bug

`Cannot create property 'declaredType' on number '1'` is an **in-process realm-pollution crash**. `runTest262File` compiles AND executes tests in the caller's own realm: `built-ins/Array/prototype/lastIndexOf/15.4.4.15-8-a-14.js` leaves `Array.prototype[1] = 1` behind (verified: the file passes ALONE; the SAME file re-run in the same process then fails `compile_error`). The next compile crashes inside the TypeScript checker's `getDeclaredTypeOfClassOrInterface` during `initializeTypeChecker`: the checker's `symbolLinks` lookup is a plain array read, so `symbolLinks[1]` inherits the polluted `Array.prototype[1]` → `links = 1` → the crash.

The sharded CI worker has had `restoreBuiltins()` for this class since #1153/#1154/#1160/#1220/#1221 (the official lane passes both cited files) — the **in-process** runner (baseline validator, smoke-tests, residual-harvest measurements like #3170's, where this was observed) had no counterpart, so harvests manufactured **order-dependent phantom compile_error records**.

- `tests/test262-restore-builtins.ts` — module-load snapshot of 12 core prototypes; deletes added keys/symbols (incl. numeric Array indices), re-assigns changed data values with a descriptor-reapplication fallback (#1160 pattern), reports non-configurable residue. The worker's version stays untouched (coupled to fork-recycle); unification is #3182 territory.
- Entry call in `runTest262File` (each in-process run starts from restored builtins).

body:
## What

Three connection-resilience changes so a movie night survives the common failure modes:

- **Relay → Trystero fallback** (`transports/relay.js` + `fallbackToTrystero` in `core/connection.js`). If the relay socket never opens after two attempts (relay laptop asleep / ngrok tunnel down), we switch to the serverless Trystero path instead of staying dead. `roomId()` now seeds from the relay URL when there's no pair code, so relay-only pairs still land together in a private (non-public) room. `connect()` respects an `S.relayFellBack` flag; a fresh pair / unpair resets it.
- **Wake & network reconnect** (`onNetworkWake`, wired to `online` + `visibilitychange` in `main.js`, plus a >12s heartbeat-gap detector). Recovers immediately on network return, tab re-show, or wake-from-sleep instead of waiting out the 8s silence window (timers pause while asleep, so the old path could lag badly).
- **Trystero TURN** — the public-relay path's `rtcConfig` now includes manual TURN + any TURN creds the relay minted this session (`S.relayIce`), so the fallback call still gets a media relay on hard NATs.

## Notes

- `node --check` + a module-graph load (through the cyclic connection↔relay↔trystero imports) pass.
- Fallback triggers only on socket-never-opened (relay unreachable), not on "socket open, partner not here yet".
